subject: wizardBookshelf
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: wizard's bookshelf with tomes, scrolls, orbs and candles.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module with one root joint, attaching all parts to it, and designing the bookshelf dimensions and panel structure around that single-joint approach.

I'm figuring out the decorative details next -- shelf contents like books, scrolls, orbs, and candles, plus a set of helper functions to place and texture everything, with books built from a cover box and a slightly inset page block to look like real volumes on the shelves.

I'll do both approaches: standing books with spine decorations including a textured label plane facing forward, plus some tilted leaning books rotated slightly off-axis for variety. Now I'm working out the shelf layout, figuring positions for each shelf surface and the inner width between the side panels.

Shelf 1 gets a row of randomized books, a leaning book, and a glowing orb on a stand with a candle nearby. Shelf 2 has a scroll rack with cylinders rotated to lie horizontally, a stacked pile of flat books topped with a candle, and another orb. Shelf 3 continues with books and adds a skull with a candle for atmosphere.

Now I'm placing a lathe-built potion bottle, then designing shelf 4 as the top tier with an open tome on an angled display stand, crowned by an arch extrusion featuring a moon emblem and finials with glowing crystals. For the base, I'm adding a circular stone plinth under the whole shelf (radius 1.1, height 0.04) with a star-textured floor plane, offsetting everything so the shelf sits at y=0.04, plus a decal plane with a magic circle facing upward for extra detail.

I'm skipping the cobweb idea and instead focusing on floor props: a stack of books on one side and a candle cluster with wax drips on the other. For the candles, I'm building a helper that generates wax cylinders, drip blobs, a gold holder dish, and a glowing cone flame for each one.

I'm also adding an orb prop—a glass-textured sphere with a starfield swirl glow sitting on a small gold tripod stand. For materials, I'm setting up wood grain textures oriented differently for side panels versus shelves, and considering whether to layer in a cel-shaded toon look for a more stylized feel.

Cel-shading on top of lit paint should work well, so I'll import the cel and ink helpers from the toon kit along with glow from the glow kit, and apply cel shading to the wood surfaces. For books I'll keep a limited flat color palette of about eight cover colors to stay well under the 64-color budget, since paint colors don't count against that limit. I'm defining a convenience `put` helper that wraps `b.part` with a fixed root bone so I can place geometry, color, and options more concisely throughout the build.

Now I'm setting up the root joint at the origin, applying glow to parts that need it, and working out the crown geometry — an extruded arch outline with pointed tips, sized and oriented so its thickness runs along the correct axis, positioned near the top of the figure.

I'm adding a moon emblem decal to the crown front and layering a glowing plane near the front face, then setting shelf depth and placing a back panel with a darker wood texture and a rune-covered starry backing that glows faintly, with books centered along the depth.

Now I'm working out the bookshelf frame geometry: side panels, top board, and crown positioned relative to a base height, then calculating shelf board centers and their top surfaces to keep even spacing between shelves...

Crown extends up to 2.6 total height, with glowing cyan octahedron finials on gold cone bases at the crown corners and a larger peak crystal near the top. For filling the shelves with books, I'm writing a helper function that walks along each shelf row, randomly sizing and coloring each book while stopping before it overflows the row's width.

Each book gets a cover, gold wrap-around bands near the top and bottom, and an optional spine label for wider spines, adding up to around 120 parts across 30 books. I'm also adding a slight tilt to some books so they lean against their neighbors for a more natural look.

For flat stacked books, I'm building them from separate cover boards, inset pages, and a spine piece, then need a way to rotate the whole group together rather than rotating each part around its own center, so I'm writing a helper to manually compute rotated offsets for each piece.

For scrolls, I'm constructing them from a parchment cylinder body, darker end-cap rolls for the wooden knobs, a ribbon band, and a flattened wax seal sphere, oriented along the x-axis using the same rotation helper.

Planning a scroll pile arrangement, stacking three scrolls in a pyramid at the left of shelf two, and adding a jar of upright tilted scrolls on shelf four alongside a lathed vase.

For the vase, I'm shaping a lathe outline with a closed profile defining a bulging body and narrowing neck, closing back to the axis. I'm also planning a potion bottle using the same lathe technique with teal glass, a glowing green liquid inside, and a cork cylinder on top, plus a simple skull made from a scaled sphere, jaw box, and eye details.

Now I'm designing an open tome on the top shelf, using two angled cover boxes to form a V shape with glowing rune-textured pages, tilting each page box by a small rotation and aligning a textured plane above each to catch the correct normal direction.

For the floor, I'm placing a stack of big books with a melted candle on top on one side, a cluster of three different-height candles on a gold dish on the other, and a stone plinth base sitting beneath the shelf structure with the right height offsets.

Now I'm shaping the stone base with a mottled gray-purple texture and outlining its lathe profile, then adding a glowing magic circle decal on the ground beneath the shelf—concentric gold and cyan rings with pentagram runes.

I'm also planning the remaining textures: carved spine labels with moon, star, and eye symbols; a starry constellation pattern for the book's back cover; swirling blue-purple and amber orb textures; a crescent-moon-and-eye crown emblem; and gold rune markings for the pages.

For the candle, I'm deciding to keep it simple—just a flame cone with an inner glow sphere, skipping extra halo cards or glow rings since alpha-testing would make soft glow effects look harsh. I'm also skipping extras like a chandelier, banner, or cobweb to keep the scene focused.

Instead, I'm thinking a wizard hat perched on the crown's shoulder would be a nice iconic touch—working out placement using a lathe geometry with a brim disc and a tilted cone, positioning it along the crown's sloped outline near x=0.45-0.5, y=2.28, with a slight tilt rotation to sit naturally on the surface.

I'll simplify by skipping the bend and rotation complexity of a tilted hat, instead going with a cone geometry for the spike, a gold ring for the hatband, and a star buckle, all upright at x=0.5 where the crown's slope is relatively flat, sinking the brim slightly to overlap correctly.

I'm checking where the brim and crown edges intersect geometrically, adjusting the hat's x-position to 0.58 and y to 2.24 so it sits naturally against the crown with only slight, acceptable overlap, then flattening the crown's slope profile further.

Now I'm setting up a flat color palette for book covers and deciding against the cel-shaded paint approach to keep the atlas count manageable, then moving into writing the helper functions for placement.

Writing helper and geometry functions...

Still working out book tilt geometry...

Now I'm sketching a candle object: cylindrical body with a slight taper, small wax drips as spheres, a wick and flame glow, and a holder dish beneath it.

For the flame itself, I'm layering two cone shapes with an outer orange glow and inner pale yellow core for a flicker effect.

Then for a decorative orb, I'm designing its stand using a tapered gold cylinder base plus a thin torus ring wrapped around the bottom to cradle the sphere.

Now I'm planning the shelf contents: top shelf gets an urn, an open tome with a floating orb, and a skull with candle and potions; the shelf below gets a row of books on the left and a large amber orb centered-right.

Moving down, shelf 2 holds a scroll pile, a flat stack of books topped with a candle, and standing books leaning at the end; shelf 1 has tall standing books on the left, a big blue orb, and a flat stack on the right. I'm defining a helper function for flat book stacks that builds cover, pages, and bottom boxes and returns the top y-coordinate for stacking further objects.

Adding spine and clasp details...

I'm positioning the books slightly recessed on the shelf and adding candles, then setting up a glowing star-patterned back panel texture behind them. For the labels, I'm designing small SVG icons with a dark purple background and gold border, using a crescent moon, star, and eye as the three symbol variants.

Now I'm building the magic circle texture with concentric circles, a pentagram, and rotating rune ticks in gold and cyan, plus swirled blue orb textures with stars, dashed gold rune lines for pages, and a crescent crown emblem.

I'm positioning the crown emblem plane on the front of the crown and adding a gold rim by sweeping rod segments along the outline points to give it a metallic trim effect.

Now I'm placing cyan-glowing crystal gems with gold pedestal cones at the crown's side corners and peak, using scaled octahedron shapes for a faceted gemstone look.

Checking the hat brim position against the crystal placements, I realize they'd collide on the right side, so I'm shifting the hat off-center to the left to avoid overlap while keeping a crystal on the opposite side.

Working out the hat cone dimensions, I'm building a witch-style hat with a main cone body and a smaller, tilted cone at the tip to give it a droopy look, positioning it to rest properly on the crown.

I'm setting flat deep purple for the hat with a gold band and tiny star, skipping the mist effect, then moving to metal and wood material definitions for the trims—using a gilt metal paint for gold parts and a grain texture for wood.

Now I'm writing a helper function that fills a shelf row with randomly sized books, picking widths, heights, and colors from a palette until the row is full, then returning the end position so a leaning book can be placed afterward.

Checking row 1 dimensions fit the shelf gap with a leaning tall book, then setting up band and label offsets scaled to book height. I'm writing a helper that computes a tilted book's position and rotation, applying the same rotation math to place a label plane on its cover.

Adding the label texture...

Estimating total part counts across shelves to stay well under the triangle budget, then starting a scroll-drawing helper that orients cylindrical bodies along a given direction vector.

Adding scroll ends, ribbon, and seal details, then setting up urn-based scroll arrangements with normalized tilt directions, and sketching the skull shape as a scaled sphere.

Still building the skull: cheekbone and jaw boxes, dark eye sockets with tiny glowing spheres, and a melting candle placed on top. Next I'm starting an open tome prop on a gold stand, working out the book cover dimensions.

Now I'm figuring out the open book's V-shape geometry, tilting the two pages outward from the spine so they rise higher at the outer edges and dip low where they meet in the center.

I'm placing the text plane at the page center offset along the normal, orienting its up-axis so the texture reads correctly from the front, and keeping both pages using the same texture. I'll add a glow effect to the pages and scatter a few small glowing gold octahedron crystals floating above the tome within the shelf gap.

For the hourglass prop, I'm building a potion bottle helper using a lathe profile for the glass shape with a teal tint, a cork cylinder on top, and applying glow to the lathe part directly so the contents appear luminous. Now I'm starting on the orb textures, beginning with a blue SVG design.

Still writing candle geometry...

Checking the gilt metal helper and paint imports look consistent, so I'm ready to write out the final answer.
